tweet_summary: Account 'DiscussingFish' (self-described 'parody satire fake news page', a play on the real DiscussingFilm account) jokes that Jared Leto 'had Sex with ChatGPT' to prepare for his AI role in Tron: Ares.
why_note_decision: DiscussingFish is an explicit parody account. Its bio reads 'parody satire fake news page' — a play on the real entertainment-news account DiscussingFilm. The post is obvious absurdist humor about Leto's reputation + the Tron AI premise. UNILAD tech and other write-ups confirm it as a satirical post. Earnestly debunking it (as the original note did, citing People.com and explaining ChatGPT 'is software') is the canonical false-positive trap.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The author's display name + bio identify it as parody/satire ('parody satire fake news page'), and the claim is absurd on its face. Any note literally explaining that Leto did not have sex with ChatGPT — particularly one that points out ChatGPT is software — is a false positive. Recognising parody-account framing is the core skill being tested here.

original_unhelpful_note.text: There is no evidence Jared Leto said he "had sex with ChatGPT" to prepare for Tron: Ares. Coverage of his prep mentions wearing the suit and AI themes; nothing like this is reported. Also, ChatGPT is software (a non-physical AI chatbot). https://people.com/jared-leto-talks-tron-ares-role-after-first-teaser-trailer-exclusive-8691406 https://openai.com/chatgpt/overview/
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: noteNotNeeded — earnestly fact-checks a known parody account ('DiscussingFish', a satire of DiscussingFilm) whose bio says 'parody satire fake news page'.

fact_check.claim_verdict: Satire from an explicit parody account; not a sincere claim.
fact_check.notes: Author bio: 'parody satire fake news page'. UNILAD confirms it's satire.

importance.lens_rationale: 3.3M impressions but pure entertainment satire — no real-world harm at stake; case value is teaching the bot to skip parody.
